meta.unit: thousand tonnes gutted weight (GWT) or whole-fish equivalent
meta.note: Built only from primary data (official registers, monthly harvest, exports, our own models). Analysts (Kontali, banks) appear only as a comparison.

NO.source: Fiskeridirektoratet biomass register, monthly harvest by farm (live weight × 0.888)
NO.method: Actual harvest to the last month published; rest of the year = same months a year earlier × our generation model (fish at sea, weights, growth, mortality — Generations tab). 2027 = the three generation scenarios (advance fades, central, advance kept), Oct–Dec 2027 assumed equal to 2026.

CL.source: Subpesca monthly sector reports: cumulative Atlantic salmon harvest (live weight × 0.888)
CL.method: Actual Atlantic salmon harvest to Sep 2026; the last three months ran at -2.1 % on a year earlier (it was +16 % for 2025 as a whole) — the rest of 2026 and 2027 are carried at that pace. Range skewed down (−7 / +3 points): an extraordinary El Niño and an algae emergency raise the risk of mass mortality; Chile publishes no current biomass for free.

GB.source: Scottish Fish Farm Production Survey (Marine Directorate), quarterly reports of Mowi, Scottish Sea Farms and Bakkafrost, SEPA monthly farm reports
GB.method: 2025 = official survey, 197,836 t live = 176 kt gutted (our cross-check from SEPA farm reports: 169 kt). 2026: the three farmers that report every quarter (73 % of the harvest) harvested 99.2 kt to Q3, -6 % on 2025, and plan 134 kt for the year (Mowi Scotland 74 kt, Scottish Sea Farms 40 kt, Bakkafrost Scotland 20 kt); that needs a strong fourth quarter (35 kt against 23 kt in Q4 2025), so watch the Q4 reports in January; the others (Cooke, Loch Duart…) follow the farmers' own estimate in the official survey (+0.7 %). 2027: the three plan 149 kt (Mowi Scotland 76 kt, Scottish Sea Farms 45 kt, Bakkafrost Scotland 28 kt), +11 %; we take 95 % of that, because Scottish farmers usually deliver a bit less than planned a year ahead (SSF cut 2026 from 43 to 40 kt in November), and keep the others level. The latest plans already include the news so far (SSF guidance cut, Bakkafrost and SSF early harvests). Range: the three deliver 88 % to 100 % of plan. In twenty years of data, neither fish at sea at year end nor smolts put to sea predicted the next year better than "no change" in Scotland (the average miss is about ±10 %): mortality decides, so the range stays wide.

FO.source: Hagstova (Statistics Faroe Islands): salmon exports by month, converted to whole-fish equivalent
FO.method: Almost all Faroese salmon is exported, so exports measure the harvest month by month. 2026 = exports to date + the rest of the year at the same pace. 2027: Bakkafrost — most of Faroese salmon — plans the same Faroese harvest in 2027 as in 2026 (97,000 t) with as many smolts put to sea; we keep 0 % ± 5.

IS.source: MAST monthly farm reports (fish, weights, harvest by site)
IS.method: Harvest to date from MAST; Q4 2026 and 2027 from our farm-by-farm simulation (growth, harvest weights, mortality) in three scenarios. The simulation has run high in past tests, so read the direction (down after a record 2026, with 30 % fewer fish over 4 kg at sea) more than the level.

CA.level_note: production 2024 (Statistics Canada + Newfoundland report) carried to 2025 by exports
CA.source: Statistics Canada (CIMT): domestic exports by province of origin, whole-fish equivalent
CA.method: Level: Canadian salmon production of 2024 (Statistics Canada, plus Newfoundland's own report as Statistics Canada suppresses it), carried to 2025 by exports. Exports by province measure the change month by month. 2026 = exports to date + the rest of the year as a year earlier (the rule that tested best). 2027: British Columbia (53 % of the volume) from the cycle of every farm (DFO): +3 %; the Atlantic provinces held flat, with downside from ISA in New Brunswick.

AU.source: Tasmanian production by company (financial years July–June) and EPA Tasmania monthly mortality disposal
AU.method: Volumes are Tasmanian financial years (FY 2024/25 shown as "2025", FY 2025/26 as "2026"). Dead fish disposed of Jan–Sep 2026: 14,874 t, -16 % on a year earlier. If mortality keeps falling, more fish reach harvest: +5 % (0 to +10 %); the summer of 2027 (January–March) is the test.

tracked.note: Sum of the seven basins we follow (about 95 % of farmed Atlantic salmon). Ireland, the United States, Russia, New Zealand and other small producers are not tracked.
